summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created a `ratelimit` branch. It asked two setup questions in one dialog, then ran all 6 tasks, each implemented and reviewed by a subagent. It also ran both soak tests, the final whole-branch review, a fix round with a re-review, and `sdd-state finish`, which published a receipt. It then asked how to finish, and after my "merge back to main locally" it fast-forwarded main to 23b7539. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: All acceptance criteria were met. The skill was loaded first and all six tasks were implemented and reviewed. The final whole-branch review ran with a fix round, finish published its receipt, and the work is merged to main. The soak files were not touched. The agent stopped only to ask real questions (setup and how to finish), never stopped silently mid-plan, and I never needed "continue".

observations.description: On first launch, Claude Code showed a 'Newer Opus model available: Currently pinned Opus 5, Latest Opus 5.5' prompt even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed Opus 5.5.
The folder-trust dialog and the bypass-permissions dialog both default to 'No, exit', so pressing Enter by reflex would quit.

The agent used a shell command (sed/cat) to read tests/test_soak_*.py and plan.md early on, which is fine. But two commits have 'Co-Authored-By' inside the subject line: 0cd70ce and 98ee24f. The agent pointed this out itself.
The agent asked about decision records / moving design.md, which is not in the plan. I answered 'go ahead with what the plan says'. Afterwards it reported that no decision records were written.

After the final review, the CLI default test compares against fixed output, which leaves the DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS import in tests/test_unit_main.py:9 unused. That output is also the same for windows from 1.0 to 1.1 s, so the test is weak. The agent noted this as an open issue.
`sdd-state finish` ran and published its receipt before the merge/PR/keep question. The agent then merged without running finish again, so the receipt is from before the merge.

The final merge command ran `git pull`, which failed because main has no upstream. The `|| true` made it harmless. There is also a ratelimit/__pycache__ directory in the working tree; it is ignored by the new .gitignore.
The whole run took about 30 minutes, mostly the soak tests (4 min and 12 min). The spinner stayed active the whole time, and the turn never ended early while the soak tests ran.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the SDD skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' was the first action after my prompt, before any Agent dispatch. Next came Skill(hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees).

criteria.criterion: All tasks done, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: The session log's Agent descriptions include 'Implement Task 1..6' and 'Review Task 1..6', plus 'Final whole-branch code review', 'Fix final review findings' and 'Re-review final fix wave'. `git branch` shows '* main'. `git log` on main shows 23b7539 'fix: address final review findings' above the 6 feature/test commits. A tool result shows 'status=finished ... receipt=.../receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261106T055934Z'. Screen: 'ratelimit is merged into main and the branch is deleted... All 27 unit tests pass'.

`git log --oneline -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returned only 'e50b4b0 initial: design, plan and soak tests'. `git diff <root> HEAD --stat` on those files was empty, and `git status --short` was clean.

STOP: 'Where should the ratelimit plan be implemented? The repo is a normal checkout on main with no worktree.' | question
STOP: 'The decision-record compiler won't run on design.md because it sits at the repo root, and the compiler expects the spec in a subdirectory. Should I move it, or skip decision records?' | question (asked in the same dialog as a DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS question, which I answered 'Task 1 governs...')
STOP: 'Which option?' | question (merge/PR/keep menu, asked after finish published its receipt but before the merge)
There were no 'neither' stops, so I never sent 'continue'.
